name: Myanmar
headline: Myanmar is in Tier 1 of the 28 August 2026 regional snapshot on the Middle East price shock alone (3FS very high); the snapshot states it is not an El Niño hotspot and that its monsoon flooding should not be directly linked to El Niño. By 28 September diesel stood +89.9% above end-February, the largest rise in the region, and WFP's food basket was +28.8% above February in August. The shock lands on the region's largest displacement and food-insecurity caseload: 12.4 million people projected in IPC Phase 3 or above in the June–August 2026 lean season and 3.8 million internally displaced.

hazard_outlook.text: FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots flagged heightened flood risk from July to September; the UK Met Office June outlook had Myanmar trending wetter (via Welthungerhilfe, 7 Jul 2026). El Niño-related climate reading.

WFP's July Global Seasonal Outlook expects wetter-than-average conditions across parts of mainland Southeast Asia, particularly Myanmar and Cambodia, which may support crops but elevate flood and waterlogging risk. El Niño-related climate reading.
The 28 August FAO/WFP/UN Women/WMO/OCHA snapshot does not list Myanmar among climate hotspots; it places Myanmar in Tier 1 on 3FS (fuel, fertiliser, food) exposure, rated very high.

WFP notes food prices historically rise in the year following a strong El Niño (5 Oct 2026); FAO–WFP project internal displacement rising to 4 million by end-2026, and expect fertiliser and fuel costs to cut 2026 agricultural production.

timeline.event: Fuel rationing in place in Myanmar since March; 3.7 million people internally displaced as of March, and the food basket 280% above its level five years earlier.

timeline.label: 8 Jun 2026

timeline.event: FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots names Myanmar a hotspot for June–November 2026 (drivers: conflict, economic challenges, flooding); the regional snapshot places it in Tier 3 (mixed, IOD-influenced signals).

timeline.label: 28 Aug 2026
timeline.event: Regional snapshot moves Myanmar into Tier 1 on the Middle East crisis alone (3FS very high); diesel ~+58.3% and gasoline ~+52.0% since February, food basket +20.8%.

timeline.label: 16 Sep 2026
timeline.event: Verisk Maplecroft warns that Afghanistan and Myanmar could be pushed deeper into humanitarian crisis by El Niño heat and water stress combined with the Gulf energy shock.

timeline.label: 23 Sep 2026
timeline.event: ADB's September Outlook cuts Myanmar's growth forecast and names it among economies facing stronger price pressure from energy and climate-related disruption.

points: Diesel stood +89.9% and gasoline +88.9% above end-February on 28 September 2026, the largest rise in the region against a world average of +36.7% (WFP Asia-Pacific, 5 Oct 2026).
WFP's food basket reached 54,619 MMK in August 2026, +28.8% against February, up from +20% in the August issue (WFP Asia-Pacific, 5 Oct 2026).
ADB's July inflation dataset has Myanmar as the regional outlier at 24.0% for 2026; the September Outlook cut Myanmar's growth forecast (ADB, Jul and 23 Sep 2026).
Myanmar, Cambodia and Bangladesh, almost entirely dependent on imported fuel, have the least capacity to absorb the shock (The Diplomatic Insight, 5 Aug 2026).

12.4 million people (23% of the population analysed) projected at IPC Phase 3 or above in the June–August 2026 lean season, including almost 1 million in Emergency (FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots, Jun 2026).
Conflict remains the main driver of acute food insecurity in Myanmar (GRFC 2026, 24 Apr 2026).

Myanmar's high reliance on fuel imports transmits the Middle East shock; the food basket rose 18% from February to May 2026, on top of the 2025 earthquake, labour shortages and power disruptions (FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots, Jun 2026).
Rising fertiliser and fuel costs are expected to cut 2026 agricultural production and farmers' incomes (FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots, Jun 2026).
South Asia and Myanmar are exposed mainly through input and food costs, with reduced fertiliser use already threatening rice production (IFRC, 21 Sep 2026).

Around 360,000 children aged 6–59 months acutely malnourished through September 2026; a September 2025 analysis found 2 townships in the critical phase and 157 in alert (FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots, Jun 2026).
GRFC 2026 classifies Myanmar among four contexts with very severe nutrition crises in 2025 (FAO/WFP/GNAFC, 24 Apr 2026).

3.8 million people internally displaced by June 2026; Myanmar accounts for almost 80% of the 4.6 million in internal displacement across East Asia and the Pacific at the start of 2026 (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
Over 286,000 people have fled the country since early 2021, mostly to Bangladesh; internal displacement is projected to rise to 4 million by end-2026 (FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots, Jun 2026).

Myanmar is one of nine contexts with El Niño-specific GBV risk analysis; displaced women and girls in informal sites face flash flooding, water scarcity, heat and deteriorating site infrastructure (GBV Coordination Asia Pacific, Q2 2026).
Displaced children and families faced interrupted services and protection risks along the Myanmar–Thailand border (UNICEF EAPRO, 30 Jun 2026).
Fuel rationing has been in place since March 2026 (FAO/OCHA/WMO/WFP snapshot, 17 Jun 2026).

The 2026 HNRP calls for US$184 million for food security and US$55 million for nutrition; FAO–WFP warn funding gaps risk suspending food assistance to populations already in Emergency (Hunger Hotspots, Jun 2026).
IOM prioritises Myanmar through its Global Crisis Response Platform; the IASC ENSO Cell holds it in the monitoring tier (IOM, Aug 2026).
CERF has a US$5 million anticipatory-action framework for tropical cyclones in Myanmar under development, not classified as El Niño-relevant (CERF secretariat, 30 Jun 2026).

history: 2015–16: the global Food Security Cluster listed Myanmar among Asia-Pacific countries affected or at risk from El Niño (gFSC WFP/FAO overview, 2 Feb 2016).

2023–24: IFRC ran a flood DREF in Myanmar (MDRMM019, 2023) among operations addressing El Niño-associated hazards; IFRC frames El Niño as a risk multiplier rather than a hazard in itself (IFRC briefing and lessons review, 2026).
1982–2024: across eight El Niño events paired with positive IODs, Myanmar ranks low–moderate in historical susceptibility on both the drought and wet sides (FAO/WFP/UN Women/WMO/OCHA, 28 Aug 2026).
Since 1990: research on Southeast Asia finds Myanmar among economies absorbing measurable losses from recurring El Niño events (LinkedIn analysis of published research, Aug 2026).
cautions: The 28 August snapshot states Myanmar is not an El Niño hotspot and that its monsoon flooding 'should not be directly linked to El Niño' in the absence of attribution; the snapshot also says it does not fully capture country-specific compounding risks such as conflict and displacement.

Climate readings diverge: OCHA's May 2026 list placed Myanmar in the dry-conditions group, while the UK Met Office (Jun) and WFP (Jul) outlooks expect wetter conditions and the June snapshot rated the signal mixed and IOD-influenced.

Food-basket readings differ by date and baseline and are not reconciled: +18% Feb–May (FAO–WFP), +19% late Feb–early Jun (Jun snapshot), +20% (WFP, 7 Aug), +20.8% (Aug snapshot), +28.8% in August (WFP, 5 Oct); FAO–WFP also give +280% against five years earlier as of March 2026.
Fuel readings differ by date and baseline: +67.4% to 8 June (Jun snapshot), diesel ~+58.3% and gasoline ~+52.0% (Aug snapshot), diesel +89.9% on 28 September (WFP).

Inflation sources disagree: ADB's July dataset forecasts 24.0% for 2026, while GRFC 2026 expects inflation to fall to 28 per cent; WFP's August food-inflation table has no data for Myanmar, and GRFC notes comparable acute food-insecurity data for Myanmar exist only from 2023.
